name: Kathmandu
source: position: Kathmandu Durbar Square (27°42'16"N 85°18'26"E); the OpenStreetMap city node sits on a hill edge, 240 m higher. Height: English Wikipedia infobox, 1,400 m; sources give 1,280 to 1,400 m for the valley floor, so the tolerance is 150 m. Checked 2026-10-18.

name: Timure
source: position: docs/specs/flash-flood-replay.md (S1); height: the elevation label of the climate table on English Wikipedia, 1,900 m, not a survey. A gorge and a label rather than a survey, so the tolerance is 200 m. Checked 2026-10-18.

name: Syabrubesi
source: position: docs/specs/flash-flood-replay.md (S2); height: trekking itineraries give 1,450 to 1,600 m, most often 1,460 m (gotonepal.com Langtang trek). A gorge, so the tolerance is wider. Checked 2026-10-18.

name: Betrawati
source: position: docs/specs/flash-flood-replay.md (Hub); height: about 600 m for Uttargaya/Betrawati (The Rising Nepal on hamropatro.com), 630 m at the DHM station there. Checked 2026-10-18.

name: Trishuli
source: position: docs/specs/flash-flood-replay.md (S3); height: no direct figure found; 622 m is the surveyed altitude of Shree Trishuli Pra.Vi. school in Nuwakot (World Bank GPSS), nearby and in the same river valley. Checked 2026-10-18.
